s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic skin eruption with atypical lymphocytic infiltrate
salient_findings: Multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules on the buttocks
Atypical lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis with eosinophils and plasma cells
key_facts: Male patient in his 70s
Eruption duration of 5 years
Previous treatments with oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, and UV-B phototherapy failed
History of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks
Syphilis screen results were negative
Molecular analysis of the T-cell receptor gamma gene showed a weak clonal band
Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement
Biopsy findings of dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes
Epidermotropism identified in second biopsy
Eosinophils and plasma cells present in the dermal infiltrate

s4.champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma

raw.champion: Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma
raw.rationale: The presence of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes and the specific clinical presentation are more closely aligned with Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma, a subtype of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, which includes Mycosis fungoides.

rejected.label: Mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: While Mycosis fungoides is a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, the specific details provided, such as the absence of epidermotropism in the initial biopsy and the presence of eosinophils and plasma cells, suggest a more specific diagnosis within the cutaneous T-cell lymphoma spectrum.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This is too broad as it encompasses several entities including Mycosis fungoides and Primary cutaneous CD4+ small/medium T-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with more papular lesions and a different immunophenotypic profile, not closely matching the described dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ lymphocytes.

rejected.label: Cutaneous pseudolymphoma
rejected.why: The presence of clonal T-cell populations and the specific histopathological findings argue against a pseudolymphoma, which would not typically show such atypical lymphocyte infiltrates.
